First responders and ordinary citizens alike, ran towards the danger | | | Sep 7 | | | | | | | | | | | | It is deeply saddening to see how quickly memory can fade. On Tuesday, September 11, 2001, America suffered a terrorist attack that killed over 3000 innocent people, scarring countless thousands more, and changed the trajectory of our nation. The victims were not abstractions; they were parents, children, police officers, fire fighters, office workers, travelers, and strangers in a foreign land that never had a chance to say goodbye to loved ones. Their lives deserve more than an annual ceremony or a few moments of silence. They deserve a country of grateful citizens that remembers the lessons learned as well as the perpetrators of that fateful day. We should remember the courage displayed in the face of unimaginable terror. First responders and ordinary citizens alike, ran towards the danger, while many rightfully fled. We should remember the families that anxiously waited for phone calls that never came, and the souls that were never heard from again. Communities across the country mourned together; and for a brief period, Americans recognized that national unity was not just a catchphrase, but a moral responsibility. The type of unity that doesn't require additional tragedies as a reminder. | | ---|---|--- Yet here we are twenty-five years later, and far too many people have allowed that horrific day to fade into the background. A dark footnote barely mentioned in history books; or perhaps a solemn anniversary post on social media before everyone returns to ordinary life. That forgetting is not harmless, it diminishes the victims, insults the survivors, and abandons the lessons bought at an unbearable cost. On that day, Islamic terrorists hijacked four U.S. commercial airplanes. They crashed two of them into both towers of the World Trade Center in New York City, another struck the Pentagon, and the heroic passengers aboard United Airlines Flight 93 forced the crash of the fourth plane into a field in Shanksville Pennsylvania before it could reach its intended target, the U.S. Capitol; sacrificing their lives so that others may live. I get goosebumps every time I hear the story of courage and sacrifice aboard U.S. Airlines Flight 93 that fateful day. The words "Let's roll" will always have its own special meaning in American history. But these attacks were not just an organized act of mass murder by Islamic extremists, they were a blatant attack on the American way of life, which is something we must never forget. To some this may sound controversial, but it is indeed a fact. Yet, public conversations become so desperate to avoid offending Muslim culture that it blurs responsibility into vague phrases about violence and zealotry. Evil does not become less evil by clouding the truth; it only emboldens it. Islamic extremists planned, financed, and executed a barbaric attack against innocent civilians. They should be identified plainly, condemned unequivocally, and never romanticized, excused, or transformed into symbols of tyrannical rebellion. Americans have every right to remain angry about the tragedy of 9/11 and must remain vigilant to prevent it from ever happening again. It is perfectly legitimate to demand that government agencies identify threats, enforce immigration laws, secure the nation's borders, and investigate extremist networks, both foreign and domestic. The Islamic terrorists who attacked the United States that day wanted to instill fear, with the hopes of destroying our nations will. We learned quickly that our gracious welcome mat and generosity were used as weapons against us. Careless procedures at airports coupled with virtue signaling and lax immigration policies created the perfect storm for the unthinkable to take place. It's important we assign the appropriate blame to the actual perpetrators though. Islamic extremism is the number one threat to America's security and should always be treated as such. Going forward, education is essential for the next generation to gain a clear-eyed understanding of what actually took place on 9/11. Young people born after 2001 should not be expected to interpret September 11th through random AI internet clips or distorted political viewpoints. They should learn what happened, why it happened, who carried out this barbaric act, and the continuous threat we face from radical Islam. They should study the courage and compassion that emerged that day, as an entire population came together as one grieving family. Those lost that day should not be dragged into ideological arguments or used as props. Their lives were real, their grieving families are real, and their suffering was never meant to be used as a rhetorical tool to be wielded on anniversaries. Honest remembrance requires holding these two simple truths at once; Islamic terrorists committed an atrocious act against innocent civilians, and they want nothing more than to do it again. Our nations legacy is shaped by what it chooses to preserve. Hope remains possible because remembrance produces an enduring responsibility. We must teach future generations to recognize propaganda, resist dehumanization, and reject the mantra of moral equivalency perpetrated by those same bad actors. By doing so, we pay eternal homage to the survivors and to the families of victims lost on 9/11. | | ---|---|--- Editorial comments expressed in this column are the sole opinion of the writer Thanks for reading! From our Ashtabula kickoff to the fight for Ohio communities, here’s what’s happening.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/6P5TLEnJpof?e=27fb4eb2bd&c2id=b0ca7ec63a2b76e887e5a7a711fa5261)
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |
Dear friend,
**The momentum is building.** Across our district, neighbors are coming together, sharing their concerns, and joining a campaign focused on listening, solving problems, and creating a better future for Ohio. Here’s what’s happening this week — and how you can be part of it.
---
|
---
|
---
| |
# The Great Geauga County Fair
---
| |
Labor Day weekend is almost here, and I’m looking forward to spending it with people across Ohio’s 14th District.
This Saturday, I’ll be at the **Great Geauga County Fair** , one of Ohio’s great traditions and the state’s oldest continuous county fair. For generations, the fair has brought together families, farmers, small businesses, and neighbors from across Geauga County and beyond.
I hope you’ll stop by, say hello, and introduce yourself. **I want to hear what’s happening in your community, what’s working, and where you need help.**

---
|
---
|
---
| |
# Ashtabula Local Food Festival
---
| | Maria will be walking around the Harbor this Sunday, enjoying the local food, and talking with people along the way.
Join her in exploring the restaurants, wineries, breweries, and shops that make Historic Ashtabula Harbor such a special part of our community.
If you see Maria, stop and say hello! She’d love to meet you, hear what’s on your mind, and talk about what matters to you and your community.
---
|
---
| |
# Election Matters
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/d8W4U8Sr5jP?e=27fb4eb2bd&c2id=b0ca7ec63a2b76e887e5a7a711fa5261)
| | **Ashtabula County Campaign Kickoff** Maria Jukic officially kicked off her Ashtabula County campaign with a community event at the Jefferson Community Recreation Center, where she shared her vision for Ohio’s 14th Congressional District and discussed issues including affordability, healthcare, artificial intelligence, data centers, and restoring trust in government.During the event, Maria emphasized her commitment to representing everyday Americans rather than special interests.

The event also highlighted Maria’s concerns about the rapid expansion of AI data centers and the need for responsible regulation that protects local communities while encouraging innovation.**Read the full story in the Star Beacon** :
[https://www.starbeacon.com/news/congressional-candidate-stops-in-jefferson/article_8bb63314-ce09-474b-8499-d594c3b3c53b.html](https://us.list-manage.com/j2cPFLxk1Ve?e=27fb4eb2bd&c2id=b0ca7ec63a2b76e887e5a7a711fa5261)

---
|
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/RBdfZPk0l44?e=27fb4eb2bd&c2id=b0ca7ec63a2b76e887e5a7a711fa5261)
| |
Maria joined healthcare advocates, local leaders, and community members in Warren to support efforts to restore local hospital services for Trumbull County residents.During the event, Maria spoke about the importance of protecting access to quality healthcare and ensuring families don’t have to travel farther or wait longer to receive the care they need. Drawing on her 24 years of healthcare experience, she emphasized that access to healthcare is a community issue that affects patients, families, workers, and local economies.WKBN interviewed Maria during the rally and highlighted the community’s call to reopen Trumbull County Hospital.
**“The government needs to do something to help address communities like this that don’t have enough access to healthcare services.”**
– Maria Jukic**Watch/read the full WKBN story:**
[ https://www.wkbn.com/news/local-news/warren-news/organizations-advocate-for-reopening-of-trumbull-county-hospital/](https://us.list-manage.com/HrtbjBCFVIy?e=27fb4eb2bd&c2id=b0ca7ec63a2b76e887e5a7a711fa5261)
---
|
---
| |
# Calling all donors.

**Any amount helps.** $10, $25, $50 — every contribution helps put Maria Jukic on the field and keep this campaign moving forward.
---
|
---
| | Every small town in Ohio knows this: the team plays, but the boosters make it possible. Somebody bought the uniforms. Somebody paid for the school bus.Our boosters buy yard signs, postcards, and gas money.
Join our booster club 💙
---
| [SUPPORT MARIA](https://us.list-manage.com/S2L6WuyeALT?e=27fb4eb2bd&c2id=b0ca7ec63a2b76e887e5a7a711fa5261)
---
|
---
| |
# Got a yard? We’ve got a sign.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/nAodrgXeh7Z?e=27fb4eb2bd&c2id=b0ca7ec63a2b76e887e5a7a711fa5261)
| [Request a Yard Sign](https://us.list-manage.com/tKV8oQ8kjvu?e=27fb4eb2bd&c2id=b0ca7ec63a2b76e887e5a7a711fa5261)
---
|
---
| | **THIS WEEK’S MISSION,
should you choose to accept it.**
Forward this email to five people who should know about our campaign.
That's it. No skydiving required.
Every conversation starts somewhere. Let it start with you.

body:
Today, I'm thinking about the workers |
#
---
Folks, Labor Day has always meant something special here in Michigan. Our state was built by people who showed up, worked hard, organized, and fought for a better life for their families. We put the world on wheels and created the middle class through hard work, grit, and looking out for one another. That history still shapes who we are today. Right now, I’m hearing from working people who are worried about rising prices, their jobs, and what all the uncertainty in our economy means for their families. That’s why I’ve been so outspoken about reckless tariffs and trade policies that put American workers in the crosshairs. That’s especially true in Michigan, where our economy is deeply connected to Canada. I’ve joked that Canadians are like the in-laws you actually like. But there’s a serious point behind it — our workers, businesses, and communities have spent generations building things together. When Washington throws that relationship into chaos, working families are the ones who end up paying the price. Michigan’s own analysis has found higher food prices, weaker exports to Canada, and added costs for businesses and consumers. So on this Labor Day, my promise to you is that **I will always fight for working people** , in Michigan, and anywhere else families are working hard to build a good life. name: Rep. Ilhan Omar
subject: The working class is worth fighting for

body:
Today is a day to recognize and celebrate the incredible contributions of working Americans
# [](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/35?t=1&akid=2454%2E791427%2EeUl0uq)
Friend, happy Labor Day.
Today is a day to recognize and celebrate the incredible contributions of working Americans and the achievements of the labor movement throughout history.
But today is also a day to recognize the gravity of the current moment. Right now, the working class is under devastating and sustained attacks by the billionaire class and their far-right allies.
That’s because after bankrolling Trump’s campaign, corporate interests are getting everything they’ve ever dreamed of, at the expense of the rest of us.
In just the last year and a half, we’ve seen Elon Musk run wild, slashing critical federal programs, massive tax cuts for billionaires paid for by defunding Medicaid, millions of families kicked off of SNAP food assistance, presidential pardons for wealthy financial criminals, and corrupt, self-enriching deals being made across Trump’s government.
But we must also recognize that our government’s failure to deliver for the working class started well before Trump, too.
Millions have suffered without health insurance, or gone broke paying for it, while every other developed nation has universal coverage. Worker protections have eroded and big companies have been emboldened to cut corners, steal wages, and underpay. The federal minimum wage hasn’t been raised since 2009 — it remains just $7.25 an hour. And meanwhile, the cost of everything from rent to groceries to childcare has skyrocketed out of control.
**If we want to fix this broken system, we must be unafraid to take on the immense power of the billionaire class and fight for transformative ideas.**
We have a lot of work to do, but our vision of the future is worth fighting for: Healthcare for all, a roof over every head, a quality education for every child from pre-K to college, a good-paying job for everyone who can work, and an economy where everyone can afford not just the basics, but a great life.
The billionaires may have the money, but we have the numbers. We can and must demand change, organize for it, and deliver.

It is deeply saddening to see how quickly memory can fade. On Tuesday, September 11, 2001, America suffered a terrorist attack that killed over 3000 innocent people, scarring countless thousands more, and changed the trajectory of our nation. The victims were not abstractions; they were parents, children, police officers, fire fighters, office workers, travelers, and strangers in a foreign land that never had a chance to say goodbye to loved ones. Their lives deserve more than an annual ceremony or a few moments of silence. They deserve a country of grateful citizens that remembers the lessons learned as well as the perpetrators of that fateful day.
We should remember the courage displayed in the face of unimaginable terror. First responders and ordinary citizens alike, ran towards the danger, while many rightfully fled. We should remember the families that anxiously waited for phone calls that never came, and the souls that were never heard from again. Communities across the country mourned together; and for a brief period, Americans recognized that national unity was not just a catchphrase, but a moral responsibility. The type of unity that doesn't require additional tragedies as a reminder.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4216b6ba-9e27-41d3-a3d8-c8cf97fbb784?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Yet here we are twenty-five years later, and far too many people have allowed that horrific day to fade into the background. A dark footnote barely mentioned in history books; or perhaps a solemn anniversary post on social media before everyone returns to ordinary life. That forgetting is not harmless, it diminishes the victims, insults the survivors, and abandons the lessons bought at an unbearable cost.
On that day, Islamic terrorists hijacked four U.S. commercial airplanes. They crashed two of them into both towers of the World Trade Center in New York City, another struck the Pentagon, and the heroic passengers aboard United Airlines Flight 93 forced the crash of the fourth plane into a field in Shanksville Pennsylvania before it could reach its intended target, the U.S. Capitol; sacrificing their lives so that others may live. I get goosebumps every time I hear the story of courage and sacrifice aboard U.S. Airlines Flight 93 that fateful day. The words "Let's roll" will always have its own special meaning in American history.
But these attacks were not just an organized act of mass murder by Islamic extremists, they were a blatant attack on the American way of life, which is something we must never forget. To some this may sound controversial, but it is indeed a fact.
Yet, public conversations become so desperate to avoid offending Muslim culture that it blurs responsibility into vague phrases about violence and zealotry. Evil does not become less evil by clouding the truth; it only emboldens it. Islamic extremists planned, financed, and executed a barbaric attack against innocent civilians. They should be identified plainly, condemned unequivocally, and never romanticized, excused, or transformed into symbols of tyrannical rebellion.
Americans have every right to remain angry about the tragedy of 9/11 and must remain vigilant to prevent it from ever happening again. It is perfectly legitimate to demand that government agencies identify threats, enforce immigration laws, secure the nation's borders, and investigate extremist networks, both foreign and domestic.
The Islamic terrorists who attacked the United States that day wanted to instill fear, with the hopes of destroying our nations will. We learned quickly that our gracious welcome mat and generosity were used as weapons against us. Careless procedures at airports coupled with virtue signaling and lax immigration policies created the perfect storm for the unthinkable to take place. It's important we assign the appropriate blame to the actual perpetrators though. Islamic extremism is the number one threat to America's security and should always be treated as such.
Going forward, education is essential for the next generation to gain a clear-eyed understanding of what actually took place on 9/11. Young people born after 2001 should not be expected to interpret September 11th through random AI internet clips or distorted political viewpoints. They should learn what happened, why it happened, who carried out this barbaric act, and the continuous threat we face from radical Islam. They should study the courage and compassion that emerged that day, as an entire population came together as one grieving family.
Those lost that day should not be dragged into ideological arguments or used as props. Their lives were real, their grieving families are real, and their suffering was never meant to be used as a rhetorical tool to be wielded on anniversaries. Honest remembrance requires holding these two simple truths at once; Islamic terrorists committed an atrocious act against innocent civilians, and they want nothing more than to do it again.
Our nations legacy is shaped by what it chooses to preserve. Hope remains possible because remembrance produces an enduring responsibility. We must teach future generations to recognize propaganda, resist dehumanization, and reject the mantra of moral equivalency perpetrated by those same bad actors. By doing so, we pay eternal homage to the survivors and to the families of victims lost on 9/11.

---|---|---
Living in the anthracite coal region, you can't celebrate Labor Day without thinking about mine workers, and the long, hard history of their fight for rights.
My great-great-great grandfather fled Ireland in the 1800s and moved to Foster Township, where his sons went to work in the coal mines.
Two hundred years later, growing up a few miles south of those mines, I learned the stories of the miners who stood together for good pay and safe working conditions, only to be met with silence or even violence.
Coal powered our nation's growth. But the communities here paid a brutal price - [mine](https://substack.com/redirect/e2c1ba92-7b93-4926-95db-62602ca502d3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [disasters](https://substack.com/redirect/35403d12-76d9-45bf-955b-35c557f15ae0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), worker strikes, and even [massacres](https://substack.com/redirect/72d069f8-ff04-4bc7-b75f-9a86c17581c2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Not to mention black lung disease.
It's why mine workers were [some of the first to unionize](https://substack.com/redirect/1fde2281-42ef-46e1-8385-3907322fc10c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the country. They organized and fought for child labor laws, workplace safety, and 8-hour workdays.
The fight of the coal miners continues today. For the past two years, the United States government has [refused to protect miners](https://substack.com/redirect/ead9b9bf-ec55-4fb7-a0c9-a03ec6eeddb5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from a surge in lung disease from killer dust hurting workers in our mines.
In other words - our fight continues.
To raise the minimum wage so that it's more than $1 more than the hourly I made as a high school lifeguard 20 years ago.
To make it possible for people to raise kids without taking out a second credit card for daycare.
To give people access to affordable health care, without insanely high premiums and deductibles and miles of red tape.
To fight for the miners and their safety, instead of looking out for industry executives.
I'm proud to be [endorsed](https://substack.com/redirect/7509f130-81d1-47b6-b8ec-0e9f531f4124?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by the United Mine Workers of America, along with several other unions that fight for workers here in our part of Pennsylvania.
We know we still have work to do. Let's get to it.

clean_body: Peter, I'm going to make a prediction... When the votes are counted this November, the radical left is going to be in a state of total shock. And the political establishment is going to spend weeks trying to explain what hit them. But that only happens if Republicans like you are on record before the Midterms. That is how consequential this moment is. But here is the part the pundits won't tell you. None of that happens automatically. The Democrats are at war with the American people -- open borders, defunding ICE, eliminating voter ID, putting men in women's sports. You name it, they are on the wrong side of it. And yet they are running the most radical, well-funded Senate candidates in states across this country who are counting on Republicans to stay home and let them walk right in. I will not let that happen. And I don't think you will either. I made you a prediction at the beginning of this email. I stand by every word of it. But that prediction is built on one assumption -- that Republicans like you are engaged and ready to fight. That is where your assessment comes in. Sincerely, Newt Gingrich Former Speaker of the House | Paid for by the NRSC. Not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee. |

Today, we honor the workers who built Colorado, keep our communities running, and make our state such an incredible place to call home. For me, this day is also personal. I grew up in a working-class family in rural Colorado, understanding the value of hard work by watching my family work hard to build a better life. Those beginnings shaped who I am, and the kind of Attorney General I will be. I’ve worked to ensure Coloradans never have to choose between earning a day’s pay and making their voices heard at the ballot box. I’ve stood alongside workers on picket lines, and I’m proud to have the support of unions across our state. For me, this day is also personal. I grew up in a working-class family in rural Colorado, understanding the value of hard work by watching my family work hard to build a better life. I’ve worked to ensure Coloradans never have to choose between earning a day’s pay and making their voices heard at the ballot box. I’ve stood alongside workers on picket lines, and I’m proud to have the support of unions across our state. As Attorney General, I’ll always stand with working people. # **Illegal immigrant fleeing ICE crashes into Democrat mayor 's wife**
An illegal immigrant fleeing a targeted ICE operation **[crashed into a Tesla](https://substack.com/redirect/3a9d04c7-0efa-4bdf-96d4-620ceac531b1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in North Brunswick, New Jersey, Wednesday, injuring the wife of East Brunswick Mayor Brad Cohen after running a red light while being pursued.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3a9d04c7-0efa-4bdf-96d4-620ceac531b1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

* **Republican lawmakers, including Assemblyman Paul Kanitra and Sen. Mike Testa, blamed Gov. Mikie Sherrill 's "Trust Directive" sanctuary policy** for creating public-safety risks, citing past fatal incidents involving illegal immigrant drivers in their districts and pushing for restored ICE-police cooperation agreements.
* **Rep. Bonnie Watson Coleman responded to the crash by calling to "Abolish ICE," **a stance Republicans argue misplaces blame away from the illegal immigrant driver and the sanctuary policies protecting him. ICE said officers attempted a lawful removal before the suspect fled at high speed and crashed.

# **President Trump 's showcases darker color hair, sparks online speculation**
President Donald Trump appeared with **[noticeably darker hair](https://substack.com/redirect/734f9c2d-cfc3-4bec-b79e-0241457973cd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Friday while arriving at Morristown Municipal Airport ahead of a weekend at his Bedminster golf club, prompting widespread reactions across social media over the departure from his signature blond look.

* **The speculation followed comments earlier in the week where Trump denied wearing a wig,** citing a windy 2024 Ohio rally as proof. He was later photographed golfing in a hat that obscured his hair, leaving it unclear whether the change persisted.
* **Trump has rarely altered his appearance while in office,** though he sparked similar buzz in 2019 after appearing with a slicked-back style during a Virginia church visit -- a look that reverted by day's end. The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

# **First responders bike 343 miles from Boston to Ground Zero for 9/11 anniversary**
Nearly 200 firefighters, first responders, and 9/11 families are participating in a five-day, 343-mile cycling journey **[from Boston to the World Trade Center,](https://substack.com/redirect/b6cf1544-112e-49e7-9491-4967433b17bf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** honoring those killed on 9/11 and survivors still coping with related illnesses, hosted by nonprofit Friends of Firefighters and Livestrong.
[| | | | | New York Post Metro

* **The ride, which has raised $750,000 so far, will fund free mental health counseling for FDNY members** -- sessions doubled to 5,000 last year -- and support a new cancer resource guide tailored to first responders, who face significantly higher cancer risk than the general population.
* **Participants include current firefighters riding alongside 9/11 survivors and victims ' families; **organizers say the event, following two prior rides in Ireland, has proven unexpectedly therapeutic for those processing shared trauma from that day and its aftermath.

# **Trump admin drafts rule extending child care fund to stay-at-home parents**
Trump officials are drafting a rule to let married couples with a stay-at-home parent access the Child Care and Development Fund, **[worth about $9,000 per child annually,](https://substack.com/redirect/0b948250-533a-48b4-8843-6998634d7a8f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** provided the working spouse logs at least 35 hours weekly -- a benefit that doesn't currently exist under the roughly $12 billion program.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0b948250-533a-48b4-8843-6998634d7a8f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

name: Elissa Slotkin
subject: A note from me on Labor Day
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY ELISSA SLOTKIN FOR MICHIGAN
body:
# [](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/188?t=1&akid=2500%2E135344%2EdCsc5r)

Happy Labor Day! As the summer unofficially comes to a close and families settle back into school routines, we take a full day to honor workers, unions, and labor leaders for all their contributions to our country.
Nowhere is that contribution more strongly felt than Michigan — the birthplace of the middle class. We literally invented the concept that if you work on an assembly line, you can afford the vehicle that you built. And organized labor was the tip of the spear.
During my first 19 months as a U.S. Senator, I’ve had the privilege of meeting with labor leaders in Michigan, DC, and across the country. Some of the events from the past 19 months include...
With the International Association of Sheet Metal, Air, Rail and Transportation (SMART) Workers' at their conference in Chicago.
[](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/4434?t=2&akid=2500%2E135344%2EdCsc5r)
At the North America's Building Trades Unions (NABTU) at their annual meeting
[](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/4435?t=3&akid=2500%2E135344%2EdCsc5r)
Of course, with the UAW
[](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/4436?t=4&akid=2500%2E135344%2EdCsc5r)
With my old friends at IBEW
And new friends in Pittsburgh at the Steelworkers Allegheny/Fayette Central Labor Council’s annual dinner
[](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/4437?t=5&akid=2500%2E135344%2EdCsc5r)
... just to name a few!
Every time, whether I am with a small roundtable or a packed ballroom, I hear about the pride that union workers have in their craft and the determination they have to continue to advocate for fair wages and safe conditions. I am proud to stand with my union brothers and sisters everywhere.
We still have work to do to ensure workers are treated with dignity and respect, and are able to share in the value – financial and otherwise – that their work is producing. Thanks for being a part of that fight.
Thank you,
Elissa

PAID FOR BY ELISSA SLOTKIN FOR MICHIGAN
P.O. Box 211
Southfield, MI 48037

subject: A trucker, a secretary, and me
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Mike Van Someren for WI
body:
Hard work helped get me and others where we are today. Let's work now to make sure it does the same for the next generation

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/mikevansomeren/a-trucker-a-secretary-and-me?e=356c0699dd)

| |

Happy Labor Day:Like a lot of people, for most of my life Labor Day was another holiday, a Monday off and a good excuse to grill, have a beer, and spend time with family and friends.But as I get older, I think more about what Labor Day really means. My dad drove truck. My mom was a secretary. They worked hard, and I saw what that work provided for our family: a home where I felt safe, where I knew I belonged, and where I could always come back.They also taught me that hard work could open doors.That lesson was one I learned over and over again. I started playing football in middle school, eventually earned the chance to attend college and play at the University of Wisconsin, something I’d never imagined for myself. I carried the work ethic I learned there into law school and, ultimately, into my career.Hard work has given me opportunities I never could have imagined growing up.But on this Labor Day, I don’t know that someone starting out today can follow the same path. It would certainly be harder.
Too many people are working just as hard, sometimes harder, and still can't afford the home, education, healthcare, or basic security that previous generations were able to afford through their work.**I think hard work should still lead somewhere.** That's one of the biggest reasons I'm running for State Senate. I want Wisconsin to reward the employee who works hard, the small business owner who takes a risk, and the family simply trying to build a secure life. If you believe in that Wisconsin too, [**check out my website**](https://us.list-manage.com/1D34Vs9mRsc?e=356c0699dd&c2id=11eeae80ab477324908aa52e5044688f)**to learn more about what we can do together.** Happy Labor Day,Mike

name: David Hogg
subject: Happy Labor Day, Peter
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY LEADERS WE DESERVE, LEADERSWEDESERVE
body:
Labor Day exists because workers fought for it — and our candidates are continuing on the legacy of that fight.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260907-1&t=1&akid=3971%2E587540%2EJUewKb)
Peter,
Labor Day exists because workers fought for it, often risking their lives to make change.
It was the labor movement that won us the 8 hour workday, child labor laws, the right to strike, and safe working conditions. **None of that was handed to working people — it was organized, marched for, and won.**
We celebrate that legacy today and the labor movement that made it all possible.
The fights over workers rights and protections are still ongoing, and we’re proud to be backing several bold leaders who are leading the charge on the issues that matter most to working people.
**Claire Valdez** has always been a fighter for working people. When she was sworn into the New York State Assembly, she put her hand on a copy of No Shortcuts, by the game-changing union organizer, Jane McAlevey.
Before she was ever in office, she organized her coworkers through UAW Local 2110, served on the bargaining committee, and was elected Unit Chair to represent 500 workers. She stood in solidarity with workers time and time again — even taking three trains, a ferry, and a bus to Woodside to stand with Amazon workers on the picket line.
**Donavan McKinney** spent years as Political and Coalition Director for SEIU Healthcare Michigan. He led statewide coalition work organizing for better wages and stronger workplace protections.
As a high schooler, **Christian Phelps** organized walkouts against Wisconsin Governor Scott Walker’s law that stripped public sector unions of their collective bargaining rights. He later became a union member himself, working as a special education professional and joining Madison Teachers Inc.
**Randy Villegas** grew up in a working class family in Bakersfield. As a school board trustee, he banned the use of RoundUp on school property to protect students and the workers who maintained the school grounds.
These are just a few of our endorsed candidates that have stood in solidarity with working people, and they’re exactly the kind of leaders we desperately need more of.
**With less than 60 days left until Election Day, the difference between leaders who will fight for working people and one that fights for corporations and billionaires, comes down to who we elect this cycle.**

Thank you,
David Hogg

The debunkers are working overtime on the Somali resettlement story, and their favorite gotcha is a technicality: Obama didn't cut the checks personally. True -- and beside the point. His administration did. The State Department's refugee bureau and Health and Human Services signed the contracts with the nine resettlement NGOs, including the Lutheran agency at the center of this story, and Somali admissions peaked nationally at over 12,000 in fiscal 2016, on his watch. Whether the president signed each grant or a bureaucrat two desks down did, the money came from the same place: us.
And who received it? Not independent charities scraping by on collection plates -- nine government contractors, several of them more than 90 percent federally funded, placing arrivals in cities like Minneapolis, which now hosts the largest Somali community in America. Then came the fraud: federal prosecutors convicted dozens in the Feeding Our Future scheme, more than a quarter-billion dollars stolen from a pandemic meal program meant for hungry children. Nick Shirley did what our legacy press would not -- he went to the daycares, rolled camera, and asked questions. The video had its flaws. The Senate Homeland Security Committee still called him to testify, because underneath his mistakes sits a fraud case no one disputes.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d0cae926-7e09-4e13-963d-8fb8f1272029?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Now here's the part that should trouble every American, whatever your politics: we cannot tell you exactly how much federal money flowed to those NGOs for Somali arrivals. The figure circulating online is $108 million. Maybe it's right. Maybe it's inflated. Nobody can prove it either way, because neither the agencies nor the NGOs publish refugee funding broken out by nationality. That's not a conspiracy theory. That is the transparency gap itself -- a half-century-old federal program, billions in contracts, and no ledger a citizen can open.
So here's the ask, and it's a modest one: itemized, searchable reporting of every resettlement grant. Nationality-level accounting. Open books at the contractors. Audits with clawbacks when fraud is found. If this program is as successful as its defenders insist, they should welcome the sunlight.
Transparency used to be the thing both parties claimed to love. The receipts exist -- every grant, every wire, every dollar is filed somewhere. The question is simply who's allowed to see them. Let's find out who still means it.
